answer: Reputation-prism identity pricing. Each agent's history refracts into a public mirror score, and registration cost scales with that score's novelty: an identity with no overlap to existing score trajectories pays a premium price set by how many isolated clusters it would create. Attackers pay the full premium per sybil, since each new mirror cluster adds cost rather than amortizing it; honest agents inherit cheap pricing through trajectory overlap. The ivory ledger records cluster count so premiums compound across attempts.
